texts.preamble: Narayan Lal vs State on 19 July, 2016 1 In The High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B.Criminal Revision Petition No. 352/1998 Narayan lal Vs. State of Rajasthan Date of Order : : 19.07.2016 Hon'Ble Mr.Justice Goverdhan Bardhar Mr. Kapil Bissa, counsel for the petitioners. Mr. L.R. Upadhyaya, Public Prosecutor for the State. <><> < > <> The petitioner by way of present revision petition under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C. has assailed the impugned judgment dated 24.06.1998 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge No.2, Udaipur (for short, 'learned appellate Court'), in criminal appeal no. 16/1998, whereby, the learned appellate Court has maintained the conviction and sentence awarded to the petitioner by the Addl.
texts.facts: for offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 (for short, 'the Act') . Brief facts, giving rise to this revision petition are that on 18.07.89, the Food Inspector inspected the petitioner's shop at Dhan Mandi, Udiapur. It is alleged that the Food Inspector purchased 600 gm of red chilli from the shop of petitioner and sent the samples to the Public Analyst at Jodhpur. The sample was found to be adulterated and accordingly, upon obtaining sanction from the competent authority, a challan was filed before the learned trial court for offence punishable under Section 7/16 of Food Adulteration Act. The learned trial Court framed charge against the petitioner for the aforesaid offence and the accused denied the charge. The prosecution, in support of the complaint, examined two witnesses including complainant. After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statements of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded. Narayan Lal vs State on 19 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105416106/ 1 Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned trial Court, petitioner approached the learned appellate Court but the appellate Court dismissed the appeal.
texts.arguments: At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he is not challenging the conviction of the petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act recorded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned appellate court but his only prayer is for issuance of direction to the State Government to consider case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, his case for commutation of sentence can very well be considered by the Government under Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. In support of this plea, learned counsel has placed reliance on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court in the case of N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80] and Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544] Learned Public Prosecutor has not opposed the prayer in general and submitted that in some of the identical cases, directions have been issued by the Court for consideration of commutation of sentence. It is not disputed that the petitioner is not a habitual offence and therefore, the prayer to examine the case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence is acceptable. In N.Sukumaran (supra), Supreme Court examined the matter pertaining to offence under Section 7/16 of the Act on the touchstone of Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. and held : "3. The offence took place in the year 1984. Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Deva(supra) following the verdict in N.Sukumaran (supra) and taking into account the fact that incident is too old, held as under : "9. Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C. The appropriate government is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
